newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-ACT LEAD AUSTRALIAN CHARGE IN SUPER 12.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-ACT LEAD AUSTRALIAN CHARGE IN SUPER 12.

text.p: Unheralded Australian Capital Territory (ACT) emerged as a new force in provincial rugby union by surging to the top of the Super 12 tournament standings during the sixth round of matches.
ACT lead the tournament standings on 21 points after running in six tries in a 50-23 defeat of South Africa's Free State on Friday at Bruce Stadium in Canberra.

South African sides Natal and Gauteng Lions, formerly known as Transvaal, and New Zealand's Auckland are all locked on 20 points, with Natal leading the chasing pack with a superior points average. All three have a game in hand over the leaders.
ACT are largely made up of players rejected by traditional Australian heavyweights New South Wales and Queensland but have developed into an inventive and powerful squad under coach Rod McQueen.

Mercurial fly-half David Knox has been unable to cement a place in the Australian side in recent years but typified the ACT spirit in setting up two of his side's tries with unexpected switches of play and silky handling.
Knox and the ACT backline profited as their forwards dominated possession against a lumbering Free State pack.
The win also stretched ACT's unbeaten home run to nine games since the inception of the tournament last year.

Queensland, normally one of the strongest provincial sides in the southern hemisphere, recorded only their first win of the tournament when they beat New Zealand's Otago Highlanders 37-24 in an unconvincing display in Brisbane on Saturday.
Queensland took a maximum five competition points by scoring four tries, the extra bonus point lifting them alongside Otago on six points at the bottom of the Super 12 table.
New South Wales on Sunday made it a clean sweep for Australian sides when Wallaby full-back Matthew Burke scored 33 points in his side's 43-29 win over Northern Transvaal.

He scored three of his side's five tries and kicked four penalty goals and three conversions to single-handedly keep alive New South Wales' hopes of qualifying for the tournament play-offs next month.

New South Wales had languished near the bottom of the table after a disappointing start but Burke's effort saw them jump two places to eighth, one point behind New Zealand sides Wellington and Waikato. Northern Transvaal slipped back one place to 10th.
Burke was the leading points scorer in last year's tournament and so far this season has contributed 94 of his side's tally of 144 points from their first five matches.
Defending champions Auckland kept their play-off hopes on course by snatching a fortunate 29-28 win over fellow New Zealanders Canterbury on Friday.
Auckland were out-scored three tries to two and hardly lived up to their formidable reputation, but squeezed home with a 73rd-minute penalty from 42 metres out by Adrian Cashmore.
In the remaining match of the round, two penalties in the final three minutes by full-back Gavin Lawless gave Natal a hard-fought 29-24 victory over Wellington in Durban on Friday.
